concepts.def: Made at the time of the event by a witness
Made later, using primary sources for evidence
Origin and purpose of a source
When a source unfairly favours one view
A conclusion drawn from clues in the source

walkthroughs.body_html:
A primary source was made at the time — a letter, diary, photo, speech.

A secondary source was made later, like a textbook. Both can be useful; both can be biased.

Use OPCVL: Origin (who made it, when), Purpose (why), Content (what it says), Value (what we learn) and Limitations (what's missing or biased).

This is the spine of nearly every source question.

An inference reads between the lines. A WWI poster of a soldier with the words 'Your country needs YOU' isn't just an image — you can infer recruitment was urgent.

All sources have some bias. A 1940 Nazi speech and a 1940 BBC broadcast on the same event will differ — that's expected, not a flaw.
